title: A namespace map with a non-string prefix is accepted and then never matches
text_original:
- Ensure custom selectors or namespace dictionaries reject non-string keys
- Fix handling of `:in-range` and `:out-of-range` with end of year weeks
- Fix a potential infinite loop in pretty printing of compiled selector objects
text_rewritten:
We build the namespace map for prefix-qualified selectors out of a config loader, and the loader occasionally hands us a key that is not a string: an integer, a boolean, a tuple. Compiling with such a map succeeds, and from then on every prefix-qualified selector quietly selects nothing, so a one-character config typo surfaces hours later as an empty result set instead of an error at the call site.

A prefix that is not a string can never be written in a selector, so a map containing one should be refused the moment it is handed over, the same way a map with a non-string namespace URI already is. Maps whose prefixes and URIs are all strings must keep working, in both the dictionary form and the iterable-of-pairs form.

We build the namespace map for prefix-qualified selectors out of a config loader, and the loader occasionally hands us a key that is not a string: an integer, a boolean, a tuple. Compiling with such a map succeeds, and from then on every prefix-qualified selector quietly selects nothing, so a one-character config typo surfaces hours later as an empty result set instead of an error at the call site.

A prefix that is not a string can never be written in a selector, so a map containing one should be refused the moment it is handed over, the same way a map with a non-string namespace URI already is. Maps whose prefixes and URIs are all strings must keep working, in both the dictionary form and the iterable-of-pairs form.
acceptance_hint: Compiling with a namespace map that contains any non-string prefix raises TypeError; well-formed maps still compile and select as before.
